direction.premise: Sunny’s carefully arranged party is ruined by rain, then rescued by connection rather than control.
direction.dramaticQuestion: Can Sunny let go of the perfect party long enough to notice the imperfect one her friends are already giving her?
direction.theme: Real joy is not keeping every drop out; it is letting your light come back after things go wrong.
direction.externalJourney: A honeycomb mishap and Aida’s rain-warning vision lead into Sunny’s outdoor party, the storm drives everyone inside, the indoor rescue becomes a wet sticky disaster, and the group finally celebrates outside in the rain.
direction.internalJourney: Sunny moves from bright control to frantic denial, then to a quiet admission that her light feels gone, before choosing to rejoin her friends in a muddy, rain-soaked version of joy.
direction.relationshipChanges: Sunny begins by treating friends as guests to impress, then as helpers to command, and ends by receiving them as the actual party. Luna becomes the friend who sits beside her instead of fixing her; Keen turns an earlier indoor failure into shared play; Howey crowns the mess with kindness.
direction.emotionalCurve: Playful mischief opens the episode, shifts to Aida’s quiet concern, rises into Sunny’s bright confidence, accelerates into soggy panic and sticky chaos, drops into a rain-softened stillness, then warms into communal release.
direction.comedyCurve: The comedy starts with catapult misfire and bee blame, escalates through wet decorations, muddy toes, a honey-pot helmet and an out-of-control dance, then relaxes into affectionate puddle play and one final Fuzzby bump.
direction.setupPayoffMap: Keen’s homemade contraption and Fuzzby’s honey hunger set up the closing honeycomb button. Sunny’s insistence on perfect sunshine sets up the rain-party inversion. The indoor do-si-do disaster pays off as Keen’s outdoor puddle song. Luna’s glimpse of the purple crystal pays off with Fuzzby discovering it the hard way. The soggy crown shifts from ruined decoration to loved token.
direction.visualMotifs: Honey gold, rain drops, drooping garlands, muddy footprints, soggy crowns, reflected images breaking in water, and crystals turning rain into prisms.
direction.sonicMotifs: Soft rain taps, honey squelches, lantern fizz, muddy splashes, Fuzzby’s crash rhythm, Sunny’s bright C-note motif dimming to amber then returning, Luna’s lavender F-note settling the scene.
direction.climax: Sunny’s fake smile finally falls in the wrecked cave, then outside on the log she admits the cost of trying to make everyone feel bright.
direction.resolution: Sunny and Luna let golden and lavender light meet in the rain; friends join, the failed party becomes a muddy square dance, and Sunny loves the worst crown because it was given with care.
direction.intendedFinalFeeling: Warm, splashy relief with the ache still visible in the rain and the soggy crown.

storyTruth.falseBelief: If the party is not bright and perfect, she has failed her friends.
storyTruth.practicalWant: Keep the party decorations, weather and guests under control.
storyTruth.keyRelationship: Sunny and Luna, with the wider friend group becoming the proof that the party was never the decorations.
storyTruth.emotionalFearOrWound: Sunny fears her light only matters when she can make everyone else happy.
storyTruth.transformedAction: Sunny stops forcing the party to look sunny and runs into the muddy rain with her friends.
storyTruth.themeProvenThroughAction: Joy becomes real when Sunny allows the ruined party to be played with instead of repaired.

transformationMap.believes: Fun means pulling off the clever trick or the perfect plan.
transformationMap.feels: Bright, mischievous, sure the world can be arranged.
transformationMap.does: Keen misfires, the bees react in character, and the honeycomb chaos plants a world where mistakes can become play.
transformationMap.relationshipCondition: Friends tease, blame and recover without anyone being cast as bad.

transformationMap.believes: Aida senses that Sunny’s perfect day may not survive what is coming.
transformationMap.does: Aida reads the broken water reflection and chooses to move toward Sunny’s day.
transformationMap.relationshipCondition: Aida protects by witnessing first, not controlling the outcome.
transformationMap.audienceFeeling: A small cloud over the fun.

transformationMap.believes: Sunny can out-brighten the rain if she moves fast enough.
transformationMap.does: She relocates the party inside and commands everyone to recreate the outside exactly.
transformationMap.relationshipCondition: Friends help her, but she cannot yet receive their care.
transformationMap.audienceFeeling: Funny pressure with a visible wobble underneath.

transformationMap.believes: If she admits the mess, everyone will see the party has failed.
transformationMap.does: She turns a honey-pot accident into a fake dance, smiling too hard as the room slips out of control.
transformationMap.relationshipCondition: The group tries to play along, but Sunny’s performance separates her from them.
transformationMap.audienceFeeling: Big laughs that start to pinch.

transformationMap.believes: Her effort to make everyone bright has made everything worse.
transformationMap.does: After Fuzzby collapses and the others stare, Sunny’s smile fades; outside, she sits with the soggy crown and lets the loss show.
transformationMap.relationshipCondition: For the first time she is not hosting anyone; she is simply beside Luna.

transformationMap.believes: The day can be loved without being fixed.
transformationMap.does: Sunny leans into Luna, touches her crystal, lets her real glow return, and accepts the rain as part of the party.
transformationMap.relationshipCondition: Luna sits with her; Howey, Misty, Keen and Amie join without demanding perfection.

transformationMap.believes: A party is the friends playing together, not the weather obeying.
transformationMap.feels: Bright again, but softer and truer.
transformationMap.does: Sunny jumps into the puddle dance wearing the soggy crown while Fuzzby’s honey quest provides the final comic echo.
transformationMap.relationshipCondition: Sunny belongs in the mess with everyone else.

tapestryMap.physicalMotifArc: Careful aiming and straightening give way to slipping, splashing and finally chosen stomping; control becomes play.
tapestryMap.visualMotifArc: Perfect rows, still reflections and straight garlands collapse into droops, drips, puddles and prisms, with the soggy crown becoming the emblem of accepted imperfection.
tapestryMap.colourAndLightJourney: Golden brightness opens the day, grey rain drains it, cave light becomes muddy and sticky, then lavender and gold combine outside into prism warmth while the rain remains.
tapestryMap.sourceSoundArc: Snaps, splats and bee crashes lead into plinks, rain pour, squish, muddy splashes, a held silence, then rhythmic puddle stomps.
tapestryMap.musicMotifArc: Sunny’s C motif starts bright and busy, thins during panic, rests almost bare at the log, then returns intertwined with Luna’s F as a gentler shared glow.
tapestryMap.environmentalMetaphor: The world refuses to stay arranged: water breaks the reflection, rain ruins the decorations, mud receives the dancers, and the same weather that spoiled the party becomes its music.
tapestryMap.openingImage: A golden honeycomb above a homemade catapult, with Keen aiming too carefully and Zenny peacefully unaware nearby.
tapestryMap.finalImage: Friends dancing in the rain while Sunny’s crystal glows warm beneath a floppy soggy crown, with Fuzzby dazed by the newly noticed purple crystal in the background.
tapestryMap.transformedMeaning: Rain shifts from the enemy of Sunny’s joy to the surface on which her real joy can be seen.

northStar.theme: Real joy is not keeping every drop out; it is letting your light come back after things go wrong.
northStar.childClearWant: Keen wants to get the honeycomb with his clever machine and not get caught.

scenePurposeAndEmotionalChange.purpose: Open the episode with real-space mischief rushing around Zenny's stillness, letting Keen's empty machine become the delayed consequence of his own cleverness.
scenePurposeAndEmotionalChange.dramaticQuestion: Can Keen's clever plan get the honeycomb without consequence, or will the world make the cost visible?
scenePurposeAndEmotionalChange.entry: If I build the clever machine and aim carefully, I can control the outcome and stay hidden from blame.
scenePurposeAndEmotionalChange.exit: He tries to save face with “It almost worked” while the damaged empty catapult tips and collapses beside him.

pointOfView: Zenny as the still measuring point while Keen's mischief crosses the space toward her.
Keen's escalating consequence measured against Zenny's still authority.

dramaticBeats.beginning: Keen's precise plan stops being private mischief and lands visibly on Zenny; the catapult cup becomes empty and Zenny carries the berry mark.
dramaticBeats.development: The comb leaves Keen's paws, bounces and rolls to Fuzzby on the near bank; Keen is exposed and hurt only by his own mechanism.
dramaticBeats.turn: Fuzzby appraises the machine, Keen claims it almost worked, the damaged machine tips/collapses, and Zenny gives one knowing wink before returning to meditation.
dramaticBeats.landing: The scene lands in warm comic calm: no lecture, just a look that says Zenny saw all of it.

performanceDirection.principalPerformance: Keen is precise then instantly evasive; Zenny is marked but knowingly composed; Fuzzby wakes into exuberant laughter without leaving the whole comb.
performanceDirection.physicalPerformance: Keen narrows his aim, releases one loaded shot, then ducks beside the now-empty machine. The berry crosses the real creek distance and splats once on Zenny’s forehead. Zenny absorbs the hit with a tiny eye reaction, controlled cleanup and still reset while Fuzzby wakes into exuberant body-laughter on the whole comb.

contract.playableIntention: Keen wants his clever plan to work without being caught; Zenny wants to keep ownership of her calm; Fuzzby turns the accident into delighted shared comedy before noticing any consequence.

phases.observableAction: Keen lines up the loaded catapult from the near bank, commits to the release, then immediately drops low beside the empty cup as the berry leaves him behind.
The oversized blueberry travels across the creek and makes one direct forehead contact, creating one visible splat and residual berry mark on Zenny.
Fuzzby wakes on the whole hanging comb and laughs with chest, head, wings and antennae all bouncing in uneven bursts while remaining supported by the comb.
Zenny opens her eyes, registers Fuzzby, licks away juice with measured control, then returns to a still seated pose with the berry mark still visible.

contract.physicalCauseAndEffect: One release empties the catapult cup; the berry’s flight ends in one forehead splat on Zenny; the impact and Fuzzby’s laughter draw Zenny out of meditation, but her controlled cleanup restores stillness without removing the mark.
contract.visibleEmotionalTurn: The visible change is from Keen’s careful confidence to hiding, and from Zenny’s meditation to marked awareness, then back to chosen composure.
contract.requiredLanding: End held on Zenny on her original leaf, calm again with the residual berry mark; Fuzzby remains on the whole hanging comb; Keen stays offscreen by the empty machine with empty paws.
contract.performanceFreedom: Allow small variations in Keen’s duck, Fuzzby’s laugh rhythm, wing flutter and Zenny’s micro-blinks, provided there is only one launch, one splat, no grab, and Zenny’s recovery stays restrained.

characterTruths.canonTrait: Scene contract trait: over-careful confidence under pressure becomes evasive self-protection when his plan misfires.

performanceDirection.principalPerformance: Keen moves from opportunistic stealth to panic to embarrassed dignity; Fuzzby shifts from distracted laughter to offended pursuit to satisfied ownership; Zenny withholds judgement until the final wink.
performanceDirection.physicalPerformance: Keen slips past Zenny with visible clearance, removes the whole comb and flees. Fuzzby loses the perch, catches himself on fast wings and pursues. Keen glances back, rushes too close to the empty machine, gets one tail snap, drops the comb, then tries to stand tall as the damaged prop gives way. Zenny finishes with one small wink and a quiet reset.

contract.playableIntention: Keen wants to turn distraction into victory, then preserve dignity after the machine exposes him; Fuzzby wants the comb back and then enjoys the returned prize; Zenny waits until the chaos has spent itself before giving one controlled acknowledgement.

phases.observableAction: Keen checks Fuzzby’s distraction, chooses the clear path past Zenny, reaches the far-tree branch, takes the whole removable comb and turns back toward the near bank.
When the comb is removed, Fuzzby drops from the lost perch, catches himself with fast irregular wings, fixes on Keen and pursues across the same route.
Keen glances back, tightens into panic, passes too close to the empty catapult, recoils from one tail contact, and loses the comb as it bounces and rolls to Fuzzby.
After the near-bank aftermath and soft machine collapse, Zenny turns from the offscreen result toward camera, gives one clear wink, closes both eyes and resumes meditation on the original leaf.

contract.physicalCauseAndEffect: Keen’s removal of the whole comb takes away Fuzzby’s support, causing Fuzzby to catch himself and pursue. Keen’s return path brings his tail into the still-tensioned empty arm or cord; one release snaps his tail, his recoil releases the comb, and the comb’s weight carries it through a bounce and roll to Fuzzby. The damaged empty machine later tips down softly after the exchange.
contract.visibleEmotionalTurn: Keen visibly shifts from sneaky opportunity to chased panic to embarrassed dignity; Fuzzby shifts from displaced pursuit to satisfied possession; Zenny shifts from watchful stillness to a single knowing acknowledgement.
contract.requiredLanding: End on Zenny alone on the original leaf, residual berry mark matched from S1.SH1, both eyes closed after one wink; near-bank consequences remain true offscreen: Fuzzby has the whole comb and Keen is beside the collapsed empty machine.
contract.performanceFreedom: Allow chase cadence, wing jitter, comb bounce spacing, Keen’s recovery posture and listener micro-reactions to vary, but preserve clear Zenny clearance, whole-comb ownership, empty-cup visibility, one tail contact, one machine collapse and one final wink.

performances.speaker: Zenny
performances.exactDialogue: OK, Fuzzby, calm down. It’s not that funny.
performances.voiceIdentity: Canonical registered Zenny voice; retain existing approved Audio1 sample, no new re-performance implied.
performances.dramaticIntention: Gently bring Fuzzby back from helpless laughter while protecting her own dignity after the splat.
performances.subtext: I know this is funny, but I am choosing not to give you the satisfaction of seeing me crack.
performances.relationshipTarget: Fuzzby, with a tiny private awareness of Keen offscreen.
performances.emotionalEntry: Freshly splatted but centered; a small eye reaction has already happened, and she is actively settling herself.
performances.emotionalExit: Composed again, berry mark still visible; laughter has been contained, not defeated.
performances.pace: Unhurried and controlled; let the restraint be funnier than annoyance.
performances.rhythm: Soft command on “OK, Fuzzby,” then a measured settling phrase; “It’s not that funny” lands drier and smaller.
performances.pauses: Tiny practical pause after “Fuzzby,” as she licks/cleans berry juice and decides not to escalate.
performances.breaths: Quiet nose breath before “OK”; no big sigh, no exasperated huff.
performances.nonVerbalActions: Zenny holds still on the original leaf, absorbs the forehead splat, tiny eye reaction, controlled cleanup, resets into meditation while Fuzzby’s authorised laughter SFX continues below her words and tapers.

performances.physicalActionRelationship: Voice supports the body’s stillness: she is marked and cleaning up, but the vocal control proves she has not lost herself.
performances.expectedTiming: S1.SH1 5.00–9.68s; Fuzzby laughter SFX underneath, mixed below intelligibility and tapering by line end.

beats.sourceScript: Keen’s over-careful catapult plan misfires onto the one character least interested in chaos. The joke belongs to Zenny’s restraint and Fuzzby’s delighted lack of restraint, while Keen hides from the consequence he caused.
exactDialogue: Zenny: OK, Fuzzby, calm down. It’s not that funny.

orderedEvents.text: A golden HONEYCOMB hangs from a branch. KEEN has built a catapult from sticks and a bendy branch. He loads a BERRY. Steps back. One eye closed. Tongue out. He lines up the shot — aiming carefully at the honeycomb. Nearby — ZENNY sits cross-legged on a leaf. Zenny meditates. Keen fires. WHOOSH — the berry flies — SPLAT. Right onto Zenny’s forehead. Juice slowly drips down. Keen ducks for cover and hides. Zenny’s eye twitches. She opens her eyes. Looks around. Sees — FUZZBY asleep on the honeycomb. Fuzzby snores, then awakens, laughing at Zenny. Zenny calmly licks the berry juice from her face. Closes her eyes again.

orderedEvents.speaker: Zenny
orderedEvents.text: OK, Fuzzby, calm down. It’s not that funny.
Above — Fuzzby is laughing so much that Keen sees an opportunity.

dialogueOccurrences.speaker: Zenny
dialogueOccurrences.exactText: OK, Fuzzby, calm down. It’s not that funny.

beats.sourceScript: Keen seizes the opportunity while Fuzzby is laughing, but the world answers with a slapstick chain: Fuzzby drops, Keen freezes, the catapult punishes him, and the honeycomb rolls to the bee who wanted it least and most.

orderedEvents.speaker: Keen
orderedEvents.text: Uh-oh—
He rushes forward — SNATCHES the honeycomb — Fuzzby drops. BUZZ-CRASH. Keen freezes. Beat. The catapult — somehow reset — SNAPS back — THWACK.

orderedEvents.speaker: Keen
orderedEvents.text: Ow!
It smacks his tail. The honeycomb flies — bounces on a rock. Rolls across a log — stops in front of Fuzzby. Fuzzby lifts his head. Sees the honey. Looks at Keen.

shots.physicalPerformance: Keen slips past Zenny with visible clearance, removes the whole comb and flees. Fuzzby loses the perch, catches himself on fast wings and pursues. Keen glances back, rushes too close to the empty machine, gets one tail snap, drops the comb, then tries to stand tall as the damaged prop gives way. Zenny finishes with one small wink and a quiet reset.
shots.animationTiming: Fast stealth into chase, a crisp single-contact slapback, then a slower aftermath with listening reactions and a soft mechanical collapse before the final held Zenny stillness.

performanceContract.playableIntention: Keen wants to turn distraction into victory, then preserve dignity after the machine exposes him; Fuzzby wants the comb back and then enjoys the returned prize; Zenny waits until the chaos has spent itself before giving one controlled acknowledgement.

phases.observableAction: Keen checks Fuzzby’s distraction, chooses the clear path past Zenny, reaches the far-tree branch, takes the whole removable comb and turns back toward the near bank.
When the comb is removed, Fuzzby drops from the lost perch, catches himself with fast irregular wings, fixes on Keen and pursues across the same route.
Keen glances back, tightens into panic, passes too close to the empty catapult, recoils from one tail contact, and loses the comb as it bounces and rolls to Fuzzby.
After the near-bank aftermath and soft machine collapse, Zenny turns from the offscreen result toward camera, gives one clear wink, closes both eyes and resumes meditation on the original leaf.

performanceContract.physicalCauseAndEffect: Keen’s removal of the whole comb takes away Fuzzby’s support, causing Fuzzby to catch himself and pursue. Keen’s return path brings his tail into the still-tensioned empty arm or cord; one release snaps his tail, his recoil releases the comb, and the comb’s weight carries it through a bounce and roll to Fuzzby. The damaged empty machine later tips down softly after the exchange.
performanceContract.visibleEmotionalTurn: Keen visibly shifts from sneaky opportunity to chased panic to embarrassed dignity; Fuzzby shifts from displaced pursuit to satisfied possession; Zenny shifts from watchful stillness to a single knowing acknowledgement.
performanceContract.requiredLanding: End on Zenny alone on the original leaf, residual berry mark matched from S1.SH1, both eyes closed after one wink; near-bank consequences remain true offscreen: Fuzzby has the whole comb and Keen is beside the collapsed empty machine.
performanceContract.performanceFreedom: Allow chase cadence, wing jitter, comb bounce spacing, Keen’s recovery posture and listener micro-reactions to vary, but preserve clear Zenny clearance, whole-comb ownership, empty-cup visibility, one tail contact, one machine collapse and one final wink.

showrunnerJudgement: PASS. The scene keeps the governing experience intact: real creek distance, mischief moving around Zenny’s still point, and the empty catapult becoming Keen’s delayed consequence. The child-clear action remains playable without explanation, and the final after-feeling lands on quiet comic calm rather than another gag.
treatmentComparison: This matches “Still Point, Moving Mischief.” The opening wide geography is preserved; the berry travel leaves Keen behind instead of compressing space; Zenny’s restraint is treated as the comic center; Fuzzby’s laughter creates Keen’s costly opening; and S1.SH2 reorients for route clarity, whole-comb theft, chase, tail-snag cause, dignity exchange, collapse, then Zenny’s final wink. The treatment’s main experience has not been replaced by generic chase coverage.
packingJudgement: PASS. Two clips are justified: the faithful scene is approximately 38 seconds, over the 30-second provider ceiling, and the split protects a real dramatic/camera boundary between S1.SH1’s misfire-restraint unit and S1.SH2’s same-moment reoriented grab/chase/consequence unit. S1.SH2 is near-full but its six internal views are motivated by distinct information needs, not padding.
